meta.method: Tier B flood-day catalog: reports grouped by date (same day, or +/-1 day with an approx date_confidence and overlapping areas); areas geocoded with pipeline/geocode.py (Nominatim, 1 req/s, cached), with a district fallback (text after the last comma, or a known district inside the string) at confidence 'neighbourhood' for full names that fail; rain signature from events/rain_history_grid_daily.json (IMERG WAT daily totals), including the local block: rain at the flooded areas' own cells for the flood day and the day before; population-weighted rain as in catalog_ranked.json (GHSL epoch nearest the flood year); candidates matched from catalog_ranked.json within +/-1 day; promotion per docs/INTAKE_PLAN.md decision 3; flood type per report and riverine episodes (Task 28b)

grouping.adjacent_days: +/-1 day only when a date_confidence is 'approx' and areas overlap
grouping.area_overlap: same normalized name or geocoded points within 2.0 km

geocoding.district_fallback: for a failed full name: retry with the text after the last comma, or a known district name inside the string; a district followed by a route word is part of a route name, not the district
geocoding.lga_exclusion: fallbacks accept place-level hits only; LGA/boundary and highway hits are excluded
geocoding.geocoded_from: the fallback query that resolved the area (null for full-name hits)

promotion_rule.deaths: a report of the day with an explicit deaths field: non-null count, or null count with a non-null who_reported; deaths_note is '<count> dead per <who_reported or publisher> (<url>)'. The death-word regex (swept away, drowned, died, dead, killed, bodies, ...) never promotes: a hit on a report whose deaths is null or missing (including old files with no deaths key) goes to the day's deaths_review for a reader to check
promotion_rule.structure: an official cause attribution with a human cause tag (not heavy_rain/lagoon_tide/dam_release) whose cause quote names a physical structure: canal, channel, collector, drain system number, bridge, culvert, outfall or named road project

flood_type.per_report: riverine: causes include dam_release, or the text (impacts, quote, cause_quote) names the Ogun River, Oyan Dam, Owena or a 'release of water'; canal_overflow alone is not riverine. lagoon: lagoon_tide is the only non-rain cause and the text says the lagoon or tide overflowed into an area; lagoon backflow that slows drainage during rain stays pluvial. pluvial: everything else.
flood_type.per_day: riverine if any report of the day is riverine; else lagoon if any is; else pluvial. flood_type_reports counts the day's reports by their own type.

episodes.rule: riverine flood days less than 21 days apart share one episode_id (ep-<first date>-riverine); reports keep their own dates. Pluvial and lagoon days are not grouped (episode_id null).
episodes.fields: areas are the union over the episode's days; deaths_note is the first that exists (earliest day); n_outlets is distinct publishers over all the episode's reports; promote applies the day promotion rule over all the episode's reports.

impacts: Second weekend in a row: residents trapped in homes and hours in traffic after hours of downpour on Sunday. State had warned Friday that flood in Ikoyi, Victoria Island and other parts could last the weekend because of Oyan Dam release.

Rain from about 2 am Sunday into the evening; several communities taken over by flood; residents trapped in homes; traffic gridlock. Photo: flood on Ikotun-Egbeda road. Discovery Estate / Opic Isheri (Lagos–Ogun border) also described; not listed as a Lagos place.

Hundreds of communities and estates in parts of Lagos and Ogun submerged after heavy downpour and opening of Oyan Dam. Ketu and Mile 12 flooded in the last one week. As of Sunday afternoon, flood around Long Bridge almost overflowing. Commissioner: lagoon could not discharge; back flow into drainage.

Houses, shops and places of worship submerged after Oyan Dam release. Tour Monday. Six deaths as named by residents: Baba Ibeji, Baba Michael, an unidentified Egun man (three drowned Monday night when canoes hit debris/hyacinth at Kio-Kio; bodies not found); a woman bitten by a snake while boarding a floater at Unity Estate, Owode-Onirin; a mother and baby who drowned when a canoe to Maidan-Orile capsized (bodies recovered three days later). Residents using canoes; schools shut.

At least six people killed in floods in Lagos, citing Punch: three men, two women and a baby. Houses and shops submerged; businesses paralysed; schools shut; many fled. Blamed on recent Oyan Dam release in Abeokuta. Ogun-Osun River Basin Authority confirmed release because the dam filled from heavy downpours.

Photo report of ongoing inundation: cars submerged, houses with stagnant water, shops shut, school locked, residents using canoes. Called the worst recent flooding; neighbouring communities had recovered.

Residents said lives and property lost and they were sacked from homes and businesses. NTIC closed five weeks; Golden Silk International shut over four weeks; a diaper factory shut; Lasena Waters shut three weeks. Students missed school. Describes 2019 floodwaters covering a greater area than 2018 along the Ogun River.

Unidentified woman died after a building collapsed on Unity Close, Magodo; LASEMA PRO Nosa Okunbor: fence collapsed on a storey building as a result of mudslide (not logged as a flood death). Four buildings collapsed at Ashade Quarter; two rescued including a pregnant woman. Sadiku Street, Iyana Ipaja: eight-room, 23-shop building partial collapse around 11am; injuries, responders rescued victims. Abraham Adesanya Estate: floodwater slowed traffic more than an hour Jubilee Bridge to the estate junction; Awoyaya also affected. Ubi Franklin: house flooded after roof caved. Mother and daughter injured at Hassan Adejobi Street. Four buildings partially collapsed at Ashade Quarters; two women rescued including a pregnant woman. Storey building at Sadiku Street collapsed about 11am; scores injured, Oke-Osanyintolu: no life lost. Iyana Oworo flood inward Third Mainland Bridge; vehicles stuck; Ikorodu Road gridlock hours. Police spokesman Bala Elkana confirmed the girl search. Wednesday Ogudu collapse of two teenagers noted as a separate prior incident.

Yesterday's heavy downpour: Azizat, 4, swept into drainage behind No. 38 Fashola Street; house submerged. Neighbour Shade Kazeem: she missed her step into a drainage covered by flood water. NEMA acting coordinator Ibrahim Farinloye: body not recovered; floodwater runs Fashola Street through Aboru, Iyana Ipaja, Command, Ota, Agbara to the sea. Two women including a pregnant lady rescued from collapsed building at Ashade Quarters; four houses affected; No. 18 Railway Line advised to leave after two days of downpour weakened it.

Rain almost nonstop Wednesday 17 and Thursday 18 Jun; many areas including Lekki. Residents: new government road ignored houses below drainage level; no canal big enough; drains filled, water entered houses and covered streets.
